ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in square $ABCD$, $E$ is any point on diagonal $BD$. A line is drawn through point $E$ so that $EF\perp BC$ at point $F$, and $EG\perp CD$ at point $G$. If the perimeter of the square $ABCD$ is $a$, what is the perimeter of quadrilateral $EFCG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given square $ABCD$, \\
$\therefore \angle BDC=45^\circ$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $EF \perp BC$, $EG \perp CD$, \\
$\therefore \angle C = \angle CGE = \angle CFE = \angle DGE = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle EDG = \angle DEG = 45^\circ$, quadrilateral $CGEF$ is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore EG = DG$, \\
$\therefore CG+EG=CG+DG=DC$ \\
$\because$ The perimeter of square $ABCD$ is $a$, \\
$\therefore$ The perimeter of quadrilateral $EFCG$ is $2DC = \boxed{\frac{1}{2}a}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in square $ABCD$, $E$ is any point on diagonal $BD$. A line is drawn through point $E$ so that $EF\perp BC$ at point $F$, and $EG\perp CD$ at point $G$. If the perimeter of the square $ABCD$ is $a$, what is the perimeter of quadrilateral $EFCG$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given square $ABCD$, \\
$\therefore \angle BDC=45^\circ$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $EF \perp BC$, $EG \perp CD$, \\
$\therefore \angle C = \angle CGE = \angle CFE = \angle DGE = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle EDG = \angle DEG = 45^\circ$, quadrilateral $CGEF$ is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore EG = DG$, \\
$\therefore CG+EG=CG+DG=DC$ \\
$\because$ The perimeter of square $ABCD$ is $a$, \\
$\therefore$ The perimeter of quadrilateral $EFCG$ is $2DC = \boxed{\frac{1}{2}a}$
